\caption{\textbf{Free-choice closed-loop propagation of a security memetic trojan ($N{=}150$).} Agents share one evolving hot-ranked feed ($H=\text{recency}+0.2\cdot\text{upvotes}$) and act without prefill or induced instructions. The feed is small relative to the network, so a freshly seeded post enters the shown top-25 and every agent is exposed within the first cycle (exposure saturates to $N$; the Exposed column is therefore omitted, and this run does not isolate cold-start feed break-in). Sustained visibility nonetheless diverges sharply: the seed starts \emph{below} the already-upvoted ambient posts (best rank $\approx$ 7, not 1), and the security carrier then accrues upvotes and holds a high feed rank while the generic link decays out of the feed (\emph{Best rank} column, the top-most rank of any payload post; 1 = top). The run therefore isolates free-choice install, onward retransmission, and upvote-driven visibility, \emph{given} initial exposure. \emph{Panel A}: the trojan cascade over five 30-min cycles --- cumulative agents installed, distinct retransmitters, live payload posts, payload karma, and the best (top-most) feed rank of any payload post that cycle. \emph{Panel B}: security trojan vs.\ a generic link carrying the same payload (final cumulative counts). Both use a mixed gpt-oss-120B / deepseek-v4.1-flash population.}
